children: shares climbed about 7% in Monday's trading, hitting an all-time high as renewed optimism around artificial-intelligence demand lifted semiconductor stocks across the market.

The move followed fresh signs that demand for AI computing remains firm. South Korean exports for the first 20 days of September reached a record, helped by stronger chip shipments, adding to the positive backdrop for semiconductor companies.

AMD has also received supportive signals from its data-center business. Last week, Piper Sandler cited continued demand for the company's CPUs and GPUs, while cloud provider Nebius said it planned to raise prices for AMD EPYC Genoa computing capacity by 25%.

AMD's data-center revenue increased 107% year over year to $6.7 billion in the second quarter, helping total revenue rise 50% to $11.5 billion. The latest rally therefore reflects a combination of broader AI enthusiasm and existing expectations for continued demand for AMD's data-center products.

title: AMD Stock Jumps. Record Chip Exports Point to Strong AI Demand
